content.text:
Audited. User-facing cmds: `attach`, `clean`, `configure`, `enable`, `disable`, `doctor`, `explain`, `login`, `logout`, `resume`, `rewind`, `sessions` (list/info/stop), `status`, `trace`, `version`. Hidden: `trail`, `search`, `migrate`, `reset`, `git-hook`, `curl-bash-post-install`, `hooks`, `__send_analytics`.

## Problems

**Redundancy**
- `configure` + `enable` both at top. Getting-started says `configure`, but `enable` duplicates. Pick one. Keep `enable`/`disable` pair; drop `configure` or alias to `enable`.
- `reset` + `clean` overlap. Fold `reset` → `clean --shadow` flag.

**Flat namespace, no nouns**
15 top-level verbs. `git`/`kubectl` style noun-verb scales better. Checkpoints & sessions are the two real domain nouns but only `sessions` groups.

**Orphans**
- `attach` → belongs under `sessions attach`.
- `resume` → belongs under `sessions resume`.
- `rewind` → checkpoint operation. Move under `checkpoint rewind` (keep top-level alias, high-use).
- `explain` → does 3 jobs (session/commit/checkpoint). Split or move under nouns.
- `trace` → debug tool. Group under `debug trace`.

**Hidden but useful**
- `search` — semantic checkpoint search. Promote to `checkpoint search` when ready.
- `trail` — branch work-tracking, still experimental. Keep hidden until shipped.

## Proposed shape

```
entire
├── enable / disable / status / doctor      # repo lifecycle
├── login / logout                            # auth
├── session
│   ├── list / info / stop
│   ├── attach       (was: attach)
│   ├── resume       (was: resume)
│   └── current      (NEW — show active session for cwd)
├── checkpoint
│   ├── list         (NEW — replaces `explain` default)
│   ├── show <id>    (was: explain --checkpoint)
│   ├── rewind       (was: rewind, keep top-level alias)
│   ├── search       (unhide)
│   └── diff <a> <b> (NEW)
├── debug
│   ├── trace        (was: trace)
│   └── logs         (NEW — tail .entire/logs/)
├── clean [--shadow] # absorbs `reset`
└── version / help
```

Top-level aliases for muscle memory: `rewind`, `resume`, `attach` stay callable.

## Missing cmds worth adding

- `debug logs` — tail `.entire/logs/`. Users cat manually now.
- `checkpoint show <id>` — direct viewer (currently `explain --checkpoint`).
- `checkpoint diff <a> <b>` — compare two checkpoints (code + transcript).
- `session current` — which session is writing checkpoints right now in cwd.
- `doctor --bundle` — zip `.entire/logs/` + settings + `git status` for bug reports. Replaces ad-hoc "send me your logs".
- `update` — self-update if installed via curl|bash (`curl-bash-post-install` exists, no update partner).
- `checkpoint replay <id>` — re-run captured prompt against current HEAD. Big value for regression hunting.

Want me to draft plan + implementation for any subset?

- The deprecation warning format is fixed: `Warning: 'entire <old>' is deprecated; use 'entire <new>' instead.` printed to stderr, exit code unchanged.

- Update getting-started docs and `gettingStarted` constant in `root.go` to reference `entire enable` (already canonical) and remove any lingering `entire configure` references where appropriate, while keeping the deprecation alias functional.

## Testing Decisions

A good test exercises external behavior: command-line invocation, output, exit code, and observable state changes (files written, settings updated, archives produced). Tests should not assert on Cobra internals or pin specific log strings unless those strings are part of the user contract. Tests prefer `testutil.InitRepo` over raw `git.PlainInit` per CLAUDE.md, and every test calls `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state.

- **`doctor bundle`** — Produced zip exists at the printed path and contains the expected entries (logs, settings.json, git snapshot file, version info).

- Cobra wiring in `root.go` is not unit-tested; coverage comes from the alias and group children's tests.
- Existing tests for `rewind`, `resume`, `attach`, `explain`, `trace`, `search`, `sessions`, `configure`, and `reset` continue to pass against the alias surface; no new tests are added there in Phase 1.

### Prior art

- Integration tests in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/` cover hook-driven flows using `testutil.InitRepo` and `execx.NonInteractive` — the new bundle/logs tests follow the same pattern.
- Existing `explain_test.go`, `sessions_test.go`, and `clean_test.go` are the closest reference for command-level test shape.

- Phase 2 (additional deprecation warnings) and Phase 3 (hiding deprecated aliases). Scheduled for later releases once Phase 1 lands.
- Renaming or restructuring the hidden infrastructure commands (`hooks`, `git-hook`, `migrate`, `trail`, `__send_analytics`, `curl-bash-post-install`).
- Any changes to checkpoint storage, session state machine, or strategy semantics. The new `checkpoint`/`session` groups are reorganizations of existing capabilities, not new behavior.

- Changes to telemetry events. The `__send_analytics` subprocess is unchanged.
- Any refactor of `activity` or `dispatch`.

## Further Notes

- Phase 1 is intentionally additive so that `mise run test:ci` should remain green throughout. The integration test suite already invokes the existing top-level commands, which continue to work via aliases.
- The Vogon canary suite must run after the changes (`mise run test:e2e:canary`) to verify the new structure does not regress hook-driven flows; no Vogon changes are anticipated since prompt wording does not change.

- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point
- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers (Cobra commands, helpers, group roots)
- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)

- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (temporary and committed)

- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))

### Command Layout

The CLI is organized around four noun groups plus a small set of top-level
verbs. Phase 1 introduced the groups additively; the previous flat top-level
verbs remain registered as silent permanent aliases so existing scripts and
muscle memory continue to work.

- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `stop`, `attach`, `resume`, `current`
- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `show`, `rewind`, `search`, `diff`
- `agent`: `list`, `add`, `remove` (replaces flag-driven `entire configure`)
- `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`

Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
`login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`.

Permanent silent top-level aliases (kept for backwards compatibility):
`rewind` → `checkpoint rewind`, `resume` → `session resume`, `attach` →
`session attach`, `explain` → `checkpoint show` (smart-routes between
checkpoint id, commit sha, and session id), `trace` → `doctor trace`,
`search` → `checkpoint search` (hidden), `sessions` → `session` (Cobra alias).

Deprecated top-level aliases (functional, print one-time stderr warning):
`configure` → `agent`, `reset` → `clean`.

Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `migrate`, `trail`, `git-hook`,
`curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`.

Helpers used by the alias surface live in `cmd/entire/cli/aliascmd.go`
(`aliasOf`, `WithDeprecation`, `warnDeprecatedAliasOnce`). Diagnostic
subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
